Text to type: October has different special days in different countries. Halloween is on 31 October, with activities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland. Canadian Thanksgiving is on the second Monday of October in Canada. In 2026, it is on 12 October. German Unity Day is on 3 October in Germany. Halloween brings costumes and candy, Thanksgiving celebrates the harvest, and German Unity Day remembers a change in the country.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: On Halloween, people wear costumes in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland. A costume is clothing that makes someone look like another person or thing. For example, someone can dress as a witch or a ghost. Some costumes are scary, and others are funny. Adults also wear costumes and go to costume parties. At these parties, dressing up is part of the fun. Halloween is not a national day, and it is not a family harvest meal.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: Canadian Thanksgiving follows a Monday rule, not one fixed date. It is on the second Monday of October. In 2026, 1 October is a Thursday, so 5 October is the first Monday and 12 October is the second Monday. This makes 12 October the holiday date in 2026. It is a harvest holiday, celebrating food grown on farms, and a day off in most of Canada. Families sit down together for a big meal. Turkey is a common main dish, with side dishes and pumpkin pie. People give thanks for the harvest and the year. This is not United States Thanksgiving, which is in November, and it is not a costume celebration or Germany’s national day.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: German Unity Day is on 3 October. Its German name is Tag der Deutschen Einheit. It is Germany’s national day, a special day for the whole country. Germany was once divided into East Germany and West Germany. Their official names were the German Democratic Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany. After protests, the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989. On 3 October 1990, East Germany joined West Germany, and the country was one again. This joining is called reunification, and German Unity Day remembers it.

Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: German Unity Day is a public holiday, so people have the day off. Many towns have public gatherings, where people meet to mark the day together. Each year, one German state hosts the main celebration. In 2026, that state is Bremen. Its city-centre festival runs from 2 to 4 October. Berlin also has events near the Brandenburg Gate, a famous city landmark. People see flags and hear speeches about the country and its history. Costumes and a harvest feast are not part of this holiday. It is a national celebration, not a food festival or a costume day.

Reading

Part 1: Different dates and different reasons

October has different special days in different countries.

Halloween is on 31 October, with activities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

Canadian Thanksgiving is on the second Monday of October in Canada.

In 2026, it is on 12 October.

German Unity Day is on 3 October in Germany.

These dates belong to the same month, but their reasons are different.

Halloween brings costumes and candy, Thanksgiving celebrates the harvest, and German Unity Day remembers a change in the country.

Reading

Part 2: Dressing up for Halloween

On Halloween, people wear costumes in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

A costume is clothing that makes someone look like another person or thing.

For example, someone can dress as a witch or a ghost.

Some costumes are scary, and others are funny.

Adults also wear costumes and go to costume parties.

At these parties, dressing up is part of the fun.

Halloween is not a national day, and it is not a family harvest meal.

Reading

Part 3: Doors, candy, and pumpkins

Children go from door to door for Halloween trick-or-treat.

They visit neighbours and say “Trick or treat!”

The neighbours give them candy.

This activity takes children to several homes, rather than keeping them in one place.

People also carve pumpkins, cutting pieces out to make faces.

These pumpkins are called jack-o’-lanterns.

A light inside makes the face shine in the dark.

Costumes, visits, and bright pumpkin faces all help make the evening special.

Reading

Part 4: A Canadian family meal

Canadian Thanksgiving follows a Monday rule, not one fixed date.

It is on the second Monday of October.

In 2026, 1 October is a Thursday, so 5 October is the first Monday and 12 October is the second Monday.

This makes 12 October the holiday date in 2026.

It is a harvest holiday, celebrating food grown on farms, and a day off in most of Canada.

Families sit down together for a big meal.

Turkey is a common main dish, with side dishes and pumpkin pie.

People give thanks for the harvest and the year.

This is not United States Thanksgiving, which is in November, and it is not a costume celebration or Germany’s national day.

Reading

Part 5: Germany becomes one country again

German Unity Day is on 3 October.

Its German name is Tag der Deutschen Einheit.

It is Germany’s national day, a special day for the whole country.

Germany was once divided into East Germany and West Germany.

Their official names were the German Democratic Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany.

After protests, the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989.

On 3 October 1990, East Germany joined West Germany, and the country was one again.

This joining is called reunification, and German Unity Day remembers it.

Reading

Part 6: Public celebrations in Germany

German Unity Day is a public holiday, so people have the day off.

Many towns have public gatherings, where people meet to mark the day together.

Each year, one German state hosts the main celebration.

In 2026, that state is Bremen.

Its city-centre festival runs from 2 to 4 October.

Berlin also has events near the Brandenburg Gate, a famous city landmark.

People see flags and hear speeches about the country and its history.

Costumes and a harvest feast are not part of this holiday.

It is a national celebration, not a food festival or a costume day.
